haller_lake_whole_house_interior.heading: Whole House Interior Remodel in Haller Lake
haller_lake_whole_house_interior.text1: An ADA-compliant whole-house interior remodel in Haller Lake, including the living spaces, two bathrooms, custom woodwork, and front entry.
haller_lake_whole_house_interior.text2: Project highlights include skylights in the living room, a custom wood floor vent set into the hardwood, two remodeled bathrooms, custom cabinetry and medicine cabinets, a wall-hung toilet with the tank hidden in the wall to save space, shower window and skylight details, dual shower heads, an accessibility-focused in-shower drying system, and a new front door.
haller_lake_whole_house_interior.short2: Whole House Interior Remodel in Haller Lake
haller_lake_whole_house_interior.text3: Explore the connected living spaces, custom wood details, bathrooms, accessibility features, and entry improvements completed throughout the home.

part1.small_heading: A broad interior remodel across most of the home
part1.text2: The living room photos show the scale of the interior work with finished hardwood flooring, a long open room, recessed lighting, large windows, and two skylights.

part2.small_heading: Skylights and clean finishes made the living room feel larger and brighter
part2.text2: The living room became one of the project’s defining spaces. The skylights, clean wall planes, recessed lighting, and large glass openings made the room feel bright and open, while the hardwood flooring added warmth throughout the interior.
part2.text3: This part of the project shows the value of updating the whole interior environment. The goal was not only to remodel isolated features, but to make the home feel more complete and comfortable from room to room.

part3.small_heading: A custom hardwood floor vent shows the level of finish work
part3.text2: A custom wooden floor vent demonstrates the level of care carried into the finish work. Rather than using a standard metal vent, the vent was built into the hardwood so it reads as part of the finished floor.

part4.small_heading: A three-quarter guest bath with a glass shower and bench
part4.text2: The bathroom includes a glass shower with a built-in bench, grab bars, and a custom vanity.

part5.small_heading: Custom shower windows and skylight-style openings became a key feature
part5.text2: The shower window is a unique detail. Its window-and-skylight style brings light from above and makes the bathroom feel more open.

part6.small_heading: Custom cabinets, a roll-under vanity, and built-in medicine cabinets
part6.text2: The primary bathroom has custom cabinets, a double vanity with double sinks, and medicine cabinets recessed into the wall. Part of the vanity was built so a wheelchair can roll right under it, with the sink, plumbing, and fixtures placed to make that work.

part7.small_heading: A curbless shower with grab bars, two shower heads, and a built-in dryer
part7.text2: The primary shower is curbless, with grab bars, two shower heads, and a warm-air drying system so the homeowner can dry off without a towel.

part8.small_heading: A new front door completed the interior and entry story
part8.text2: The new front door has a beautiful stain-grade finish. The natural wood adds warmth to the entry.
